lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: fractions of a whole in measurement and sharing contexts
lessonRef.title: Concept extension: fractions of a whole in measurement and sharing contexts

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example applies the idea in a new setting. Notice what stayed the same.

items.prompt: A rectangle is partitioned into 4 parts of equal area. What fraction does one part represent?

steps: 4 equal parts make up the whole.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what is different about this case before you start.

items.prompt: A shape is divided into 4 equal parts. 1 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?
A circle is partitioned into 6 parts of equal area. What fraction of the circle does one part represent?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A shape is divided into 6 equal parts. 4 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?
A square is partitioned into 6 parts of equal area. What fraction of the square does one part represent?
A shape is divided into 6 equal parts. 1 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?
A rectangle is partitioned into 8 parts of equal area. What fraction of the rectangle does one part represent?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain, in writing, what made this case different from the original one.

items.prompt: A shape is divided into 8 equal parts. 4 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A rectangle is partitioned into 6 parts of equal area. What fraction of the rectangle does one part represent?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
